demand.basis: Task side of the match: required_ability = ability_floor[difficulty] + critical_headroom + property_span * (reasoning_depth / 4) * property_load, where property_load is the weighted mean of the task properties (code_complexity/3, (context_scale-1)/2, (divergence-1)/2, (hallucination_risk-1)/2, min(error_cost,2)-1). Work without a profile uses its difficulty as the depth and default_load as the load. Each property capability requirement also grows depth_coupling per depth above 2. Supply side: model tier x that model's own effort_curves coefficient. A candidate below required_ability pays shortfall_weight per tier point (high-precision work that is not critical adds precision_headroom to its requirement); effort above High earns ability credit only up to required_ability; a window about to reset with surplus quota waives the extra burn and adds up to sprint_effort_weight for the effort step above High.

scoring.basis: Task demand is continuous: required_ability = ability_floor + critical_headroom + property_span * depth/4 * property (scoring.demand), not a depth-to-effort table. Supply is model tier x the model's own effort_curves coefficient, so any effort of any model may serve any task; medium/low are offered whenever tier + curve still clears the floor, and xhigh/max are chosen only when the demand exceeds what High saturates. Ability saturates at the required ability; minimum-sufficient work prices excess ability above required_ability + saturation_span, scaled by the effort's burn and exempting GUI/frontend at depth >= 2. High precision earns high_precision_effort_weight times positive effort ability gain above High. Opportunity cost includes displaced demand in USD plus smooth weekly scarcity below scarcity_usable_ref_pct. Observed demand behind schedule is floored at demand_pace_floor_ratio times linear pace. Near a reset, surplus earns reset_bonus_max (1.2) and waives opportunity cost, extra_effort_penalty and overqualification in proportion to sunk_weight, so expiring quota is converted into higher thinking effort. Fast-capable models (Sol/Astra) enable fast mode (2x burn) during pre-reset sprints (sunk_weight >= fast_sprint_sunk_threshold) or when speed is requested and usable quota after 2x burn remains >= fast_plentiful_usable_pct.

models.capabilities_basis: 6D vectors: benchmark-calibrated core rows retain their existing basis; newly discovered frontier rows use explicitly provisional routing priors, not measured benchmark scores. models.basis: Absolute tiers (at High effort) are provisional: derived from the ordering already in model-capabilities.md (Grok behind the leaders, Flash as volume sink). Calibrated ability order: Opus > Astra > Argon > Sonnet > Sol > Grok > Flash; Dot is Astra-powered (OpenAI documents Dot as Astra-powered), so it has Astra's tier, meets every difficulty floor and has unlimited usage. Dot is not limited to text; it has its own computer and can receive code, public data and handed-over tables and return files, so it is a candidate for every route unless the parent marks the work `needs.local_only` (`excluded_when: local_only`) or it needs vision; visual ability order is Opus 5.5 > Astra > Argon > Sol > Sonnet > Flash (the numeric `visual` values 1.0/0.8/0.75/0.7/0.6/0.3 encode that order; false means no vision). Argon shares the Antigravity Gemini pool with Flash but burns roughly 8x as much quota per hour (`burn_pct_per_worker_hour`). Fable is on hold. Correct the rest here; nothing else encodes a global ranking.
models.order_basis: Zero-to-frontier-ceiling normalization over AA v4.3.2, Bug Hunt Bench (n=2..5 runs), Terminal-Bench 2.0/4.0, Mercor BrowseComp, MMMU-Pro, OSWorld/GUI harness grounding, and Calibration sample (14d) usage-stats.json.

effort_curves.basis: Per-model effort curves. `ability` is the change in tier from High (or `ability_mult`: tier multiplier per effort); `burn` is the quota multiplier (0.7 = High; or `burn_mult`: multiplier relative to High). Effective ability = model tier x its effort coefficient; the task side is depth x property difficulty (scoring.demand), never a fixed depth-to-effort table. Efforts a model has no entry for fall back to the policy-wide `effort_ability` and `effort_burn`. `ability` is the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index change from High at each effort (independent; leaderboard of 2026-10-09) times 0.1 tier per index point; `burn` is 0.7 times the Artificial Analysis cost per task relative to High, so it carries the longer runs higher efforts need. Each entry names its `calibration_source`; recalibrate an entry by replacing its numbers and source together. Grok has no medium or max entry, Flash no low, xhigh or max.

dot_execution.scope: A bounded assignment the user's own OpenAI Dot can finish end to end and return as a completed text deliverable.
dot_execution.effort: As supported and justified by the task

web_research.scope: Gather, check and organize information from the open web or other public sources on Dot's own computer, and return a written, sourced result: surveys of options or vendors, current prices, specs or versions, documentation and changelog lookups, fact-checks, news and background roundups, comparison tables.
web_research.effort: As supported and justified by the task

text_in_text_out.scope: Self-contained work whose whole input fits in the packet and whose deliverable is text returned to the parent: drafting, rewriting, translating, summarizing, critiquing, comparing, explaining, and reviewing the logic of a document given in full (mark that `hard`).
text_in_text_out.effort: As supported and justified by the task

exploration_analysis.scope: Explore and analyze material on this machine and return findings as text, with light or no code: map how a codebase or system works, trace where and why something happens, read logs, configs, data files or documents, run read-only commands and throwaway scripts to measure something, audit or compare options against the local evidence, and check a document against the code, configuration or data it describes.
exploration_analysis.role: explorer or analyst (findings to the parent)
exploration_analysis.effort: As supported and justified by the task

research_packet.scope: Run a defined quantitative experiment, evaluation benchmark, simulation, backtest or data analysis pipeline on this machine's data. Use existing tooling or bounded experiment scripts, compare named variants against a baseline, verify statistical results and report metrics, uncertainty and reproducible artifacts.
research_packet.role: research worker (single owner of the packet)
research_packet.effort: As supported and justified by the task

self_contained_code.scope: Self-contained code and validation work whose whole input fits in the packet (the spec, interfaces and any existing source it must match; keep it to about 40,000 characters) and whose deliverable is new files with their unit tests, or a report of numbers, returned as text: a module and its tests, a script, a data-processing, backtest or validation routine.
self_contained_code.effort: As supported and justified by the task

visual_analysis.scope: Interpret screenshots, charts, diagrams, spatial layouts, image evidence or visual discrepancies; distinct from writing frontend code.
visual_analysis.effort: As supported and justified by the task

direction_reasoning.scope: Deep reasoning and discussion of solution direction, competing architectures, assumptions, causal explanations, or which problem to solve.
direction_reasoning.effort: As supported and justified by the task

complex_build_plan.scope: Turn an agreed direction into a repository-grounded multi-system build plan: dependencies, interfaces, staged migrations, sequencing, validation and rollback.
complex_build_plan.effort: As supported and justified by the task

general_implementation.scope: Implement an agreed plan, maintain production features, refactor bounded code or deliver ordinary repository changes.
general_implementation.effort: As supported and justified by the task

debug_review.scope: Subtle bug diagnosis, regression analysis, review of code and diffs, invariants, test-driven repairs and checking existing behavior.
debug_review.role: reviewer or debugging worker, as assigned
debug_review.effort: As supported and justified by the task

frontend_implementation.scope: Write UI components, interactions, animations and styling from the accepted design; visual evidence inspection is a separate visual_analysis task when material.
frontend_implementation.effort: As supported and justified by the task

bounded_bulk_work.scope: Homogeneous small changes, independent extraction or inventory, boilerplate and fixed transformations with explicit acceptance.
bounded_bulk_work.effort: As supported and justified by the task

tool_execution.scope: A bounded outcome primarily requiring file, shell, browser, API or other tool calls, with direction and authorized actions already established.
tool_execution.effort: As supported and justified by the task

computer_use.scope: Operate a graphical computer or app through screenshots, mouse and keyboard (computer use): GUI-only applications, desktop or browser flows with no API, clicking through settings.
computer_use.effort: As supported and justified by the task

other_or_mixed.effort: As supported and justified by the task
